passage.quote: Acceptance is the final authorized commit step. It verifies that the prepared proposal and its base have not changed, reuses the completed checks, and commits only that content. It does not repeat the investigation or run tests again. If the proposal changes, it must be prepared again; acceptance does not authorize a push.

links.reason: Acceptance must use the base, selected files, review, and final tree that preparation pinned.

summary: User-authorized acceptance commits the exact prepared proposal after checking its identity, base, live contents, branch state, and structural validity.
Hooks may inspect the proposal and amend its message; failures or content changes stop acceptance before the branch moves. Unrelated staged and working edits are preserved.
Interrupted acceptance can resume under the same identity. Completed tests are reused, and acceptance never pushes.
Index reconciliation changes only exact accepted paths and preserves other staged descendants. Conflicting staged ancestors or descendants stop acceptance before a commit is created.
